findings.title: Shared global SSLContext absorbs client certs and extra CAs
findings.why_it_matters: Once any request in the process uses verify=True together with cert=(...), that client certificate/key is loaded into the one module-level _preloaded_ssl_context. Every later verify=True connection, from any Session and to any host, then offers that client certificate when the server asks for one. Concurrent requests with different client certs also race on the same context, so a connection can present another tenant's identity. urllib3 treats a caller-supplied ssl_context as owned by the caller: ssl_wrap_socket calls context.load_cert_chain(certfile, keyfile) and context.load_verify_locations(ca_certs/ca_cert_dir/ca_cert_data) on it in place. The same leak applies to CA material a subclass sets through init_poolmanager (ca_certs/ca_cert_dir/ca_cert_data), which then becomes trusted process-wide. Before this change, each connection built its own context, so this could not happen. The fix is to use the shared context only when no per-pool material will be loaded into it.
findings.suggested_fix: In _urllib3_request_context, only set pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context when verify is True AND client_cert is None. When verify is True and a client cert is given, fall back to the previous behaviour (pool_kwargs["ca_certs"] = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)) so urllib3 builds a fresh per-connection context. Better still, use a per-connection copy instead of the module singleton. Add a regression test that sends with verify=True and cert=(c, k), then asserts the next verify=True pool with no cert does not share a context that had load_cert_chain called on it.
evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:95 -- pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context  (module singleton created at adapters.py:75, shared by every adapter/session in the process)
urllib3/util/ssl_.py:407-433 -- context = ssl_context ... if ca_certs or ca_cert_dir or ca_cert_data: context.load_verify_locations(...) ... if certfile: context.load_cert_chain(certfile, keyfile)

urllib3/connection.py:887-891 -- cert_file=self.cert_file, key_file=self.key_file, ... ssl_context=self.ssl_context  (HTTPSConnection.connect passes the pool's shared context plus the per-pool client cert)

src/requests/adapters.py:482-488 / 323-329 -- client_cert sets pool_kwargs["cert_file"]/["key_file"] and cert_verify sets conn.cert_file/conn.key_file on the same verify=True pool that received the shared ssl_context
urllib3/connection.py:1042 -- context.verify_mode = resolve_cert_reqs(cert_reqs)  (further in-place mutation of the shared context per connection)

findings.title: Preloaded context overrides subclass ssl_context from init_poolmanager
findings.why_it_matters: A very common pattern is an HTTPAdapter subclass that overrides init_poolmanager (or proxy_manager_for) and passes ssl_context=custom_ctx. People do this for custom ciphers, legacy renegotiation, TLS version pins, OS/truststore trust, or a private CA. With verify=True (the default), every request now silently replaces that context with _preloaded_ssl_context: PoolManager._merge_pool_kwargs lets per-request pool_kwargs override connection_pool_kw. The custom TLS policy is dropped without any error. Handshakes then fail, or verification runs against certifi instead of the intended trust store. The stated intent explicitly requires that HTTPAdapter subclass customizations not regress.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the target manager (self.poolmanager or the selected proxy manager) into _urllib3_request_context. Only inject the preloaded context when the manager's connection_pool_kw has no "ssl_context" of its own, e.g. `if verify is True and "ssl_context" not in poolmanager.connection_pool_kw: pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context`. Add a test in which a subclass passes ssl_context through init_poolmanager and the resulting pool's conn_kw['ssl_context'] is that custom context.
evidence: urllib3/poolmanager.py:400-409 -- base_pool_kwargs = self.connection_pool_kw.copy() ... for key, value in override.items(): ... base_pool_kwargs[key] = value
src/requests/adapters.py:240-245 -- self.poolmanager = PoolManager(num_pools=connections, maxsize=maxsize, block=block, **pool_kwargs)  (documented subclass hook where ssl_context is supplied)

findings.title: Import fails without ssl module or with missing CA bundle
findings.why_it_matters: Building and loading the context at module import makes `import requests` itself fail in two situations. First, on a Python built without the ssl module, create_urllib3_context raises TypeError. requests/__init__.py deliberately tolerates that case (`import ssl` / `except ImportError: ssl = None`). Second, when the certifi bundle path is missing or unreadable (for example repackaged or trimmed installs, or a broken frozen app), load_verify_locations raises at import. Before, the missing-bundle case surfaced only as a per-request OSError for verify=True HTTPS. Programs that only use http://, or that always pass verify=<path> or REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, never needed the bundle, and now cannot import requests at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the module-level initialisation in try/except (ImportError, TypeError, OSError) and set _preloaded_ssl_context = None on failure. In _urllib3_request_context, use the preloaded context only when it is not None; otherwise keep the previous per-request path (cert_verify sets conn.ca_certs to extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH) and raises the existing 'Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle' OSError).
evidence: urllib3/util/ssl_.py:223-224 -- if SSLContext is None: raise TypeError("Can't create an SSLContext object without an ssl module")
src/requests/__init__.py:121-124 -- try: import ssl / except ImportError: ssl = None  (requests explicitly supports importing without ssl)
provenance: 4089f3dc6 Agustin Borrego 2024-05-15 - Wrap line to comply with CI lint (module-level load introduced by this PR series, f21e70bf/8f954567)

findings.title: HTTPS proxy TLS now verified against OS store, not certifi
findings.why_it_matters: When an https:// proxy tunnels an HTTPS request with verify=True, the proxy's own certificate is checked with the pool's ca_certs, not the pool's ssl_context. The ssl_context is used only for forwarding proxies. Before, cert_verify set conn.ca_certs to the certifi bundle, so the proxy was verified against certifi. Now ca_certs stays None, so urllib3 builds a default context and calls load_default_certs(), which uses the OS trust store. Environments whose OS store is empty or differs from certifi can see HTTPS proxy connections start failing, or trust a different set of CAs than the target connection. Examples are python.org macOS builds without 'Install Certificates', and minimal containers without ca-certificates. This is a verify-semantics change that the intent says must not happen.
findings.suggested_fix: Assumption: HTTPS proxies should keep being verified against the requests CA bundle. In _get_connection, when a proxy is selected and verify is True, drop pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] and set pool_kwargs["ca_certs"] = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH), which is the previous behaviour for the proxied path. Proxied requests keep the old per-connection load, while direct requests get the speedup.
evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:304 -- if verify is not True:  (verify=True no longer sets conn.ca_certs; previously conn.ca_certs = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH))
urllib3/connection.py:962-968 -- ssl_context = self.ssl_context if self.proxy_is_forwarding else None ... ca_certs = self.ca_certs

urllib3/connection.py:1031-1068 -- if ssl_context is None: default_ssl_context = True ... if not ca_certs and not ca_cert_dir and not ca_cert_data and default_ssl_context ...: context.load_default_certs()

residual_risks: Thread-safety of mutating a shared SSLContext (load_cert_chain / verify_mode / check_hostname) while other threads handshake with it is not verified. The finding above covers the leak; interleaving behaviour under OpenSSL was not tested.

Subclasses that set ssl_minimum_version/ssl_version/ciphers via init_poolmanager: when ssl_context is supplied, urllib3 ignores those kwargs for the handshake. This was not run end-to-end, but it follows the same override path as the ssl_context finding.
testing_gaps: No test sends verify=True with a client cert and then checks that a later cert-less verify=True request does not reuse a context with that cert loaded.
No test checks that an HTTPAdapter subclass passing ssl_context via init_poolmanager keeps its context when verify=True.
No test covers which CA source verifies an https:// proxy's certificate when verify=True.
